title: Module flattening by an admissible blowup for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Closed and open immersions are representable and have the indicated property on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Modules are on small etale ringed sites, with quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is of finite type if etale locally finitely generated; it is of finite presentation if etale locally it has an exact presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to M\to0$ with $m,n$ finite. For a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$, write $p:T'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T\to T$ for the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, obtained by etale descent of scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Its exceptional effective Cartier divisor $E$ has ideal locally generated by a non-zero-divisor $t$. For $f:X\to T$, the module strict transform of $M$ is $M'=q^*M/\{m:t^a m=0\text{ for some }a\geq0\}$ on $X\times_TT'$, where $q$ is the projection to $X$. The space strict transform is the closed subspace cut out by this torsion ideal for $M=\mathcal O_X$. These definitions retain the centre $\mathcal K$. Let $T$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let $U\subseteq T$ be a quasi-compact open subspace, and let $f:X\to T$ be locally of finite presentation with $X$ quasi-compact. Let $M$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module such that its restriction $M_U$ to $X_U=X\times_TU$ is of finite presentation and flat over $U$. Here relative flatness means that for every etale scheme chart $A\to U$ and every etale scheme chart $W\to X_U\times_U A$, the restricted module has stalks flat over the corresponding local rings of $A$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Then there exists a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ with $\mathcal K|_U=\mathcal O_U$ such that $M'$ is of finite presentation over $\mathcal O_{X\times_TT'}$ and flat over $T'$ in the same chartwise sense. No quasi-separatedness of $f$ and no Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Tag 087C (theorem-flatten-module); strict transform convention spaces-divisors.tex Tag 0862 (definition-strict-transform).

proof.text: Choose affine schemes $V,W$ with representable surjective etale maps $a:V\to X$ and $\varphi:W\to T$ by [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement]. Since $T$ is quasi-separated, [lem-sfb-space-affine-source-qc-separated] makes $\varphi$ quasi-compact and separated. Put $U_W=W\times_TU$ and $Y=V\times_TW$. To see that $U_W$ is quasi-compact, choose by the same node an affine scheme $U_0$ with a representable surjective etale map $U_0\to U$; quasi-compactness of $\varphi$, tested on the affine $U_0$, makes $W\times_TU_0$ quasi-compact, and $W\times_TU_0\to W\times_TU=U_W$ is surjective etale as a base change [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Composing with a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme onto $W\times_TU_0$ [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], the open subscheme $U_W$ of $W$ is the continuous image of a quasi-compact scheme, hence quasi-compact. The scheme-test and composition assertions of [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests] make $Y$ a scheme and $Y\to X$ etale. The map $Y\to X\times_TW$ is surjective etale, being the base change of $a$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 087C (theorem-flatten-module), first paragraph and choice of the base atlas in the second paragraph.

proof.text: Affineness makes $V,W$ qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Thus $Y=V\times_TW$ is qcqs by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products], applied after forgetting to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. In particular $Y\to W$ is quasi-compact by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. It is locally of finite presentation by the chart test [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], since $Y\to X$ and $W\to T$ are etale. Let $N$ be the Zariski quasi-coherent module corresponding to $M|_Y$ under [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. The restriction is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. Finite type of $M$, and finite presentation of $M_U$, pass to these etale restrictions by their local-presentation definitions and to $N,N|_{Y_{U_W}}$ by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison]. The original chartwise flatness hypothesis, on the charts $U_W\to U$ and $Y_{U_W}\to X_U$, gives flatness of $N|_{Y_{U_W}}$ over $U_W$.

source.place: Tag 087C, scheme-case hypotheses for the chart $Y	o W$.

proof.text: The scheme theorem [lem-trf-flattening-module-by-admissible-blowup] applies to $Y\to W$, $N$, and $U_W$: Step 2 gives quasi-compactness, local finite presentation, finite type, and the two hypotheses over $U_W$; $W$ is affine and $U_W$ quasi-compact by Step 1. Obtain a finite-type quasi-coherent Zariski ideal $I\subseteq\mathcal O_W$, unit on $U_W$, whose blowup $c:W_1\to W$ has strict transform $N_1$ flat over $W_1$ and of finite presentation. Here the finite-type centre and its restriction are part of the admissible datum [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. Regard $I$ also as an etale ideal via [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] and [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-ideal-factor] to $\varphi:W\to T$, $U$, and $I$. All its hypotheses were checked in Step 1; $\varphi$ is etale in the chart-test sense because for etale scheme charts $a:C\to W$, $b:D\to T$ and $h:C\to D$ with $\varphi a=bh$, the maps $\varphi a$ and $b$ are representable etale, so $h$ is etale by the last clause of [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Obtain $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ and $I'\subseteq\mathcal O_W$ of finite type with $\mathcal J|_U=\mathcal O_U$ and $\mathcal J\mathcal O_W=II'$.

source.place: Tag 087C, second paragraph: scheme flattening followed by Tag 087B.

proof.text: Set $T'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}T$ and $W_2=W\times_TT'$. The flat base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties] identifies $W_2$ with the ordinary scheme blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_{II'}W$. This identification uses that $\varphi$ is etale, hence flat, and identifies the specified centre ideal as well as the map. The same node identifies $T'\to T$ with the identity over $U$, since $\mathcal J|_U=\mathcal O_U$. It is therefore the required $U$-admissible blowup of the base. Convert $I'$ and $II'$ to Zariski finite-type ideals using [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] and [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison]; their equality is unchanged, as both equivalences restrict to the identity on open sections.

source.place: Tag 087C, the blowup of the pushed-down ideal and its flat base change.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-factorized-centres-product-transform] with scheme base $S=W$, open $U_W$, original scheme $X=Y$, module $N$, and a singleton index set. Set $T_r=W$, $Y_r=Y$, $e_r=\operatorname{id}_W$, $j_r=\operatorname{id}_Y$, $\mathcal J_r=I$, $\mathcal J'_r=I'$, and $\mathcal I_r=II'$. The identities are quasi-compact and flat, the base is qcqs, and $II'$ is unit over $U_W$ because it equals $\mathcal J\mathcal O_W$. Step 3 supplies the required first flat strict transform. The cited statement identifies the strict transform $N_2$ for $II'$ with the ordinary pullback of $N_1$ along the second blowup $W_2\to W_1$, as modules on $Y\times_WW_2$, and makes $N_2$ flat over $W_2$. Since $N_1$ is finitely presented, [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-finite-presentation] makes $N_2$ finitely presented. Thus both properties survive the further blowup, including the quotient-map comparison needed below.

source.place: Tag 087C, factorization into two blowups and preservation of flatness and finite presentation; flat.tex Tag 0814 and modules.tex lemma-pullback-finite-presentation.

proof.text: On schemes the torsion quotient used in this item is the module strict transform of [def-trf-module-strict-transform]. Indeed on an affine chart with exceptional equation $t$ and module $P$, a section vanishes on $D(t)$ exactly when its image in $P_t$ is zero, equivalently when some power of $t$ annihilates it. The supported kernel is quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-locally-principal-supported-kernel]. The equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] commutes with tensor pullback, and its exactness [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] carries this kernel and quotient to the same etale torsion quotient: the just-written criterion applies on every affine etale test chart $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, because this chart is flat [def-weil-etale-morphism] and tensoring with the flat $R'$ carries $\ker(P\to P_t)$ to $\ker(P\otimes_RR'\to(P\otimes_RR')_t)$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-strict-transform-etale-localization] to $Y\to X$, $W\to T$, and $Y\to W$. It identifies the restriction of $M'$ to $Y\times_WW_2$ with the etale module associated to $N_2$, compatibly with the ordinary-pullback quotient maps.

source.place: Tag 087C, use of Tag 0863(3); scheme strict-transform interface from Tag 0862 and divisors.tex definition-strict-transform.

proof.text: The maps $W_2\to T'$ and $Y\times_WW_2\to X\times_TT'$ are surjective etale by base change of the atlases, using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the covering clause of [lem-sfb-space-strict-transform-etale-localization]. Step 6 exhibits $M'$ on this cover as the quasi-coherent, finitely presented module $N_2$; hence $M'$ is quasi-coherent by the local-presentation definition [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and of finite presentation by the finite-presentation local definition in the statement. Every point of $X\times_TT'$ has a lift to that scheme chart; there $N_2$ is flat over $W_2$ by Step 5. Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-arbitrary-charts] at each point: flatness on this one compatible source-and-target chart implies flatness on every such chart. Thus $M'$ is flat over $T'$ in precisely the required sense. This proves both conclusions without quasi-separatedness of $X$ or $f$.
